Testing Automation
==================

Overview
--------

A framework for generating and running tests across different systems and configurations, supporting both baremetal and containerized environments.

Quick Start
-----------

1. Create your user configuration file (see :ref:`configuration-guide` below for advanced configuration):

   .. code-block:: toml

      CUDA_HOME = "/path/to/cuda"
      NCCL_HOME = "/path/to/nccl"
      NCCL_TEST_PATH = "/path/to/nccl_tests"

      # SBATCH directives for job submission
      sbatch = [
         "--gres=gpu:8",
         "--ntasks-per-node=8"
      ]

2. Create your testset configuration file, or use the pre-defined ones in ``testing-automation/config/nccl/``

   .. code-block:: toml

      # NCCL Test Configuration
      description = "allreduce_algo_proto_sweep"
      library_name = "nccl"

      [[test]]
      name = "all_reduce"
      binary = "all_reduce_perf"
      envs_merge_strategy = "override"
      args_merge_strategy = "override"
      [test.sweep_envs]
      NCCL_ALGO = ["RING", "TREE", "NVLSTREE"]
      NCCL_PROTO = ["SIMPLE", "LL128"]

3. Generate a job script:

   .. code-block:: bash

      # Generate a job script and print to stdout
      nvcomms-perf generate-job-script --system CLUSTER_1 --systems-toml systems.toml --user-toml user.toml --testset-toml testset.toml

      # Generate a job script and save to file
      nvcomms-perf generate-job-script --system CLUSTER_1 --systems-toml systems.toml --user-toml user.toml --testset-toml testset.toml --output job.sbatch

      # Generate a job script with specific run type and script type
      nvcomms-perf generate-job-script --system CLUSTER_1 --systems-toml systems.toml --user-toml user.toml --testset-toml testset.toml --run-type openmpi --script-type sbatch

4. Run the job script on cluster:

   .. code-block:: bash

      sbatch job.sbatch

Command-line Interface
----------------------

Arguments
~~~~~~~~~

- ``--system``: System name (e.g., CLUSTER_1, CLUSTER_2) **[required]**
- ``--systems-toml``: Path to systems TOML file **[required]**
- ``--user-toml``: Path to user TOML file **[required]**
- ``--testset-toml``: Path to testset TOML file **[required]**
- ``--run-type``: Run type (srun, container) [default: srun]
- ``--script-type``: Type of job script (sbatch, interactive, bash) [default: sbatch]
- ``--generate-test-report``: Generate test report after all tests are completed (multiple allowed, e.g., junit)
- ``--append-config-contents``: Append the contents of the TOML files to the generated job script
- ``--output``, ``-o``: Output path for job script. Default: Print to stdout
- ``--verbose``, ``-v``: Enable verbose output

Environment Variables
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

- ``NVCOMMS_PERF_TOOLS_BINARY_SUFFIX``: Suffix to append to the binary name (e.g., "_mpi" for NCCL binaries in containerized environments). Suggested to include in user config. Can be set at run time.
- ``NVCOMMS_PERF_TOOLS_WORKSPACE``: Path to the workspace directory. Set at run time.

.. _configuration-guide:

Configuration Guide
-------------------

User Configuration
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Define your environment variables and settings in a TOML file, say ``user.toml``. The configuration supports four levels of precedence:

1. Library-specific (highest)
2. Running Environment-specific
3. System-specific
4. Global (lowest)

For most configuration values, the highest precedence level will override lower levels. However, for sbatch directives, the behavior is different:

- sbatch directives from different levels are merged in order of precedence
- This allows for combining sbatch directives from multiple levels
- For example, global sbatch directives can be combined with system-specific ones

Each config must be "name = value", they will be exported in the generated script

There are several special keywords in user configuration:

1. ``sbatch``: Each string in the list will be added as a SBATCH directive in the generated job script. SBATCH directives from different configuration levels are merged in order of precedence, allowing you to combine directives from multiple levels.

2. ``pyxis``: Each string in the list will be added as a Pyxis container parameter in the generated job script. This is only used when the run type is "container". Like ``sbatch``, Pyxis parameters from different levels are merged in order of precedence, allowing you to combine container parameters from multiple levels.

3. ``prologue_commands``: A string containing commands to be executed before the tests run. Unlike ``sbatch`` and ``pyxis``, this is not a list and follows the normal precedence rules where higher levels override lower levels.

4. ``epilogue_commands``: A string containing commands to be executed after all tests complete. Like ``prologue_commands``, this follows normal precedence rules where higher levels override lower levels.

Example user configuration with different precedence levels and sbatch/pyxis merge behavior:

.. code-block:: toml

   # Global configuration
   CUDA_HOME = "/path/to/your/cuda"
   LD_LIBRARY_PATH = "${CUDA_HOME}/lib64:${CUDA_HOME}/lib${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"

   # Global SBATCH directives
   sbatch = [
       "--job-name=nccl-test",
       "--nodes=2",
       "--ntasks-per-node=8"
   ]

   # Global Pyxis container parameters
   pyxis = [
       "--container-name=nccl-test",
       "--container-mounts=/path/to/data:/data"
   ]

   # Global prologue commands
   prologue_commands = """
   source /path/to/your/own/env/setup/script
   export PATH=${CUDA_HOME}/bin:${PATH} # you can also choose to export env vars here
   """

   # Global epilogue commands
   epilogue_commands = """
   echo "All tests completed"
   """

   [CLUSTER_1]
   CUDA_HOME = "/CLUSTER_1/path/to/your/cuda"

   # System-specific SBATCH directives
   sbatch = [
       "--partition=gpu",
       "--account=gpu"
   ]

   # System-specific Pyxis container parameters
   pyxis = [
       "--container-image=nccl-test:latest"
   ]

   # System-specific prologue commands
   prologue_commands = """
   echo "running tests on CLUSTER_1"
   """

   # System-specific epilogue commands
   epilogue_commands = """
   echo "tests completed on CLUSTER_1"
   """

   [CLUSTER_1.baremetal]
   [CLUSTER_1.baremetal.nccl]
   NCCL_HOME = "/CLUSTER_1/baremetal/path/to/your/nccl"
   NCCL_TEST_PATH = "/CLUSTER_1/baremetal/path/to/your/nccl-tests"
   MPI_HOME = "/CLUSTER_1/baremetal/path/to/your/openmpi"
   HPCX_HOME = "/CLUSTER_1/baremetal/path/to/your/hpcx"

   # Library-specific SBATCH directives
   sbatch = [
       "--gpus-per-node=8",
       "--time=1:00:00"
   ]

   # Library-specific Pyxis container parameters
   pyxis = [
       "--container-env=NCCL_DEBUG=WARN",
       "--container-env=NCCL_IB_TIMEOUT=20"
   ]

   [CLUSTER_1.container]
   NVCOMMS_PERF_TOOLS_BINARY_SUFFIX = "_mpi"

   # Library-specific prologue commands
   prologue_commands = """
   source $HPCX_HOME/hpcx-init.sh
   hpcx_load
   """

   # Library-specific epilogue commands
   epilogue_commands = """
   hpcx_unload
   """

Writing Testset Configuration
-----------------------------

The testset configuration file defines the tests to run and their parameters. Here's how to write your own configuration:

.. code-block:: toml

   # NCCL Test Configuration
   description = "allreduce_algo_proto_sweep_with_split_mask_user_buffer"
   library_name = "nccl"

   [common]
   path = "${NCCL_TEST_PATH}"

   [common.sweep_envs]
   NCCL_DEBUG = "WARN"
   NCCL_DEBUG_FILE = "nccl_debug_file.%h.%p.txt"
   NCCL_TESTS_SPLIT_MASK = ["0x0", "0x3", "0x7"]

   [common.sweep_args]
   -t = 1
   -g = 1
   -f = 2
   -n = 20
   -w = 5
   -b = "8"
   -e = "16G"
   -d = "float"
   -R = [0, 1]

   [common.sweep_custom_commands]
   pre_command = "export NCCL_MNNVL_CLIQUE_ID=$(($SLURM_PROCID / $CLIQUE_SIZE))"
   post_command = "unset NCCL_MNNVL_CLIQUE_ID"

   [[common.exceptions]]
   [common.exceptions.sweep_envs]
   NCCL_ALGO = ["NVLSTREE", "NVLS", "PAT"]
   NCCL_PROTO = ["LL", "LL128"]

   # Define test configurations for each collective
   [[test]]
   name = "all_reduce"
   binary = "all_reduce_perf"
   envs_merge_strategy = "override"
   args_merge_strategy = "override"
   pre_command = "export TEST_SPECIFIC_VAR=all_reduce_mode"
   post_command = "unset TEST_SPECIFIC_VAR"
   [test.sweep_envs]
   NCCL_ALGO = ["RING", "TREE", "NVLSTREE"]
   NCCL_PROTO = ["SIMPLE", "LL128"]

Key Components
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

1. **Global Configuration**:
   - ``description``: Description of the testset
   - ``library_name``: Name of the library being tested (e.g., "nccl")
   - ``use_default_params``: Enable/disable default parameter validation
   - ``allowed_envs_to_sweep_on_default``: List of environment variables allowed to have multiple values, only takes effect on use_default_params = 1
   - ``allowed_args_to_sweep_on_default``: List of arguments allowed to have multiple values, only takes effect on use_default_params = 1
   - ``testset_iterations``: Number of times to repeat the entire testset (default: 1)
   - ``test_iterations``: Number of times to repeat each individual test (default: 1)

2. **Common Section**:
   - ``path``: Path to the test binaries (can use environment variables)
   - ``sweep_envs``: Environment variables applied to all tests
   - ``sweep_args``: Command line arguments applied to all tests
   - ``sweep_custom_commands``: Commands executed before/after each test across all tests
   - ``exceptions``: List of exceptions to filter out unwanted combinations

3. **Test Sections**:
   - Each test is defined under ``[[test]]``
   - ``name``: Name of the test
   - ``binary``: The executable to run
   - ``envs_merge_strategy``: How to merge environment variables with common section ("override" or "merge")
   - ``args_merge_strategy``: How to merge arguments with common section ("override" or "merge")
   - ``sweep_envs``: Test-specific environment variables
   - ``sweep_args``: Test-specific command line arguments
   - ``pre_command``: Command executed before each test runs (limited to maximum 1 value)
   - ``post_command``: Command executed after each test completes (limited to maximum 1 value)

4. **Parameter Sweeping**:
   - Parameters in ``sweep_envs`` and ``sweep_args`` can be single values or lists
   - Lists generate multiple combinations through Cartesian product
   - Example:

     .. code-block:: toml

        [test.sweep_envs]
        NCCL_ALGO = ["RING", "TREE"]    # Will generate 2 combinations
        NCCL_PROTO = ["SIMPLE", "LL128"] # Will generate 2 combinations
        # Total combinations: 2 * 2 = 4
        # 1. NCCL_ALGO=RING, NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE
        # 2. NCCL_ALGO=RING, NCCL_PROTO=LL128
        # 3. NCCL_ALGO=TREE, NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE
        # 4. NCCL_ALGO=TREE, NCCL_PROTO=LL128

        [test.sweep_args]
        -n = [2, 4]    # Will generate 2 combinations
        -g = [1, 2]    # Will generate 2 combinations
        # Total combinations: 2 * 2 = 4
        # 1. -n=2, -g=1
        # 2. -n=2, -g=2
        # 3. -n=4, -g=1
        # 4. -n=4, -g=2

   - Environment variables and arguments are swept independently
   - Total combinations = product of all list lengths in sweep_envs * product of all list lengths in sweep_args
   - Single values are used as-is in all combinations

5. **Pre and Post Commands**:
   - ``pre_command`` and ``post_command`` allow you to execute shell commands before and after each individual test
   - These are particularly useful for setting up test-specific environment variables or configurations
   - Commands are executed separately on each rank/process after spawning, enabling rank-specific setup
   - Each command is limited to a maximum of 1 value (no arrays allowed)
   - Can be defined in two locations:

     a. **Common Section** (applies to all tests):

     .. code-block:: toml

        [common.sweep_custom_commands]
        pre_command = "export NCCL_MNNVL_CLIQUE_ID=$(($SLURM_PROCID / $CLIQUE_SIZE))"
        post_command = "unset NCCL_MNNVL_CLIQUE_ID"

     b. **Test Section** (applies to specific test):

     .. code-block:: toml

        [[test]]
        name = "clique_test"
        binary = "all_reduce_perf"
        pre_command = "export TEST_SPECIFIC_VAR=value"
        post_command = "unset TEST_SPECIFIC_VAR"
        [test.sweep_envs]
        NCCL_ALGO = ["RING", "TREE"]

   - In these examples:
     - Before each test: Sets up environment variables based on test requirements
     - After each test: Cleans up the environment variables
     - Common pre/post commands apply to all tests, while test-specific commands apply only to that test

6. **Merge Strategies**:
   - ``override``: Test values override common values
   - ``merge``: Common and test values are combined into a list
   - Default is "override" if not specified

   Examples:

   .. code-block:: toml

      # Common section
      [common.sweep_envs]
      NCCL_ALGO = "RING"
      NCCL_PROTO = ["SIMPLE", "LL"]

      # Test with override strategy (default)
      [[test]]
      name = "test1"
      envs_merge_strategy = "override"
      [test.sweep_envs]
      NCCL_ALGO = "TREE"     # Overrides common value
      NCCL_PROTO = ["LL128"] # Overrides common value

      # Resulting environment variables:
      # NCCL_ALGO = "TREE"     (overridden)
      # NCCL_PROTO = ["LL128"] (overridden)

      # Test with merge strategy
      [[test]]
      name = "test2"
      envs_merge_strategy = "merge"
      [test.sweep_envs]
      NCCL_ALGO = "TREE"     # Merged with common value
      NCCL_PROTO = ["LL128"] # Merged with common value

      # Resulting environment variables:
      # NCCL_ALGO = ["RING", "TREE"]     (merged)
      # NCCL_PROTO = ["SIMPLE", "LL", "LL128"] (merged)

   The same applies to ``sweep_args`` with ``args_merge_strategy``:

   .. code-block:: toml

      # Common section
      [common.sweep_args]
      -n = 2
      -g = 1

      # Test with override strategy
      [[test]]
      name = "test3"
      args_merge_strategy = "override"
      [test.sweep_args]
      -n = 4    # Overrides common value
      -b = "8M" # New argument

      # Resulting arguments:
      # -n = 4     (overridden)
      # -g = 1     (from common)
      # -b = "8M"  (new)

      # Test with merge strategy
      [[test]]
      name = "test4"
      args_merge_strategy = "merge"
      [test.sweep_args]
      -n = 4    # Merged with common value
      -b = "8M" # New argument

      # Resulting arguments:
      # -n = [2, 4]  (merged)
      # -g = 1       (from common)
      # -b = "8M"    (new)

7. **Exceptions**:
   Exceptions allow you to filter out specific parameter combinations that you don't want to test.
   They can be defined in both common and test sections, and all exceptions are combined when
   processing.

   **Key Concepts**:

   - Exceptions are defined using the same structure as ``sweep_envs`` and ``sweep_args``
   - Multiple exceptions can be defined in both common and test sections
   - An empty list ``[]`` in an exception means "match any value"
   - If a parameter exists in both ``sweep_envs`` and ``sweep_args``, both must match to exclude a combination

   **Example Configuration**:

   .. code-block:: toml

      # Common exceptions - filter out specific algorithm/protocol combinations
      [[common.exceptions]]
      [common.exceptions.sweep_envs]
      NCCL_ALGO = ["NVLSTREE", "NVLS", "PAT"]  # Match any of these algorithms
      NCCL_PROTO = ["LL", "LL128"]             # Match any of these protocols

      # Test-specific exceptions - filter out specific mask values for PAT algorithm
      [[test.exceptions]]
      [test.exceptions.sweep_envs]
      NCCL_ALGO = "PAT"                        # Match PAT algorithm
      NCCL_TESTS_SPLIT_MASK = ["0x0", "0x3"]   # Match these mask values

   **Resulting Behavior**:

   The above configuration will exclude the following combinations:

   1. Any test where:
      - ``NCCL_ALGO`` is NVLSTREE, NVLS, or PAT **AND**
      - ``NCCL_PROTO`` is LL or LL128

   2. Any test where:
      - ``NCCL_ALGO`` is PAT **AND**
      - ``NCCL_TESTS_SPLIT_MASK`` is 0x0 or 0x3

   This effectively prevents testing certain algorithm/protocol combinations that are known
   to be incompatible or not interesting for your test cases.

Best Practices
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

1. **Parameter Organization**:
   - Group related parameters together
   - Use descriptive names for tests
   - Keep common parameters in the common section
   - Use comments to explain parameter choices

2. **Sweeping Strategy**:
   - Be mindful of the number of combinations generated
   - Use arrays only when you need to test multiple values
   - Consider using exceptions to filter unwanted combinations
   - For default configurations, limit sweeping to NCCL_TESTS_SPLIT_MASK

3. **Environment Variables**:
   - Use ``${VARIABLE}`` syntax for paths and directories
   - Set appropriate debug levels (e.g., "WARN" for production)
   - Configure debug file paths for troubleshooting

4. **Pre and Post Commands**:
   - Use ``pre_command`` and ``post_command`` for test-specific setup and cleanup
   - Define common pre/post commands in ``[common.sweep_custom_commands]`` for actions needed by all tests
   - Define test-specific pre/post commands directly in test sections for test-unique requirements
   - Always pair setup commands with corresponding cleanup commands
   - Keep commands simple and focused on single operations
   - Use environment variable cleanup in post commands to avoid test interference

5. **Documentation**:
   - Add comments explaining parameter choices
   - Document any special requirements or dependencies
   - Note any known issues or limitations
   - Include examples of generated commands

Troubleshooting
---------------

1. **Missing Configuration Files**: Ensure all required configuration files are present in the ``config`` directory.
2. **Invalid System Name**: Check that the system name provided matches a system defined in ``systems.toml``.
3. **Invalid Run Type**: Ensure the run type is one of: ``srun`` or ``container``.
4. **Environment Variable Conflicts**: Check for conflicts in environment variables defined in different configuration files.

Convert Command
===============

Overview
--------

The ``convert`` command is used to convert test results (from tarballs or individual test outputs) to a local file in the specified format (such as CSV).

Quick Start
-----------

Convert test results to a local file:

.. code-block:: bash

   # Convert a single NCCL test output to a local CSV file
   nvcomms-perf convert -i nccl-tests:/path/to/nccl-tests.log -o results.csv

   # Convert test results from tarball to a local CSV file
   nvcomms-perf convert -i tarball:/path/to/archive.tar.gz -o results.csv

   # Convert multiple test result sources to a single local CSV file
   nvcomms-perf convert -i tarball:/path/to/archive1.tar.gz -i tarball:/path/to/archive2.tar.gz -o combined_results.csv

   # Specify output format explicitly
   nvcomms-perf convert -i nccl-tests:/path/to/test.log -o csv:/tmp/results.csv

   # Hide progress bar
   nvcomms-perf convert -i tarball:/path/to/archive.tar.gz -o results.csv --hide-progress

   # Stop on first error
   nvcomms-perf convert -i tarball:/path/to/archive.tar.gz -o results.csv --stop-on-error

   # Use custom number of parallel workers
   nvcomms-perf convert -i tarball:/path/to/archive.tar.gz -o results.csv --max-workers 8

Command-line Interface
----------------------

.. code-block:: bash

   Usage: nvcomms-perf convert [OPTIONS]

     Convert test results to a local file in the specified format.

   Options:
     -i, --input INPUTFILE           Input file(s) to convert.

                                     Supported input types: nccl-tests, tarball
                                     Format: <type>:<path> Example: nccl-tests:/path/to/nccl-tests.log
                                     Multiple input files can be specified by using --input multiple times. Each input file will be processed and combined into the final output.  [required]
     -o, --output OUTPUTFILE         Output file path to write the converted results.

                                     Supported output types: csv
                                     Format: <type>:<path> OR <path> Example: csv:/tmp/results.csv , /tmp/results.csv
                                     If type is not specified, it will be inferred from the file extension.  [required]
     --max-workers INTEGER           Maximum number of parallel workers for parsing. Default: MIN(number of CPU cores, number of input files)
     -p, --show-progress / -P, --hide-progress
                                     Show progress bar during parsing  [default: show-progress]
     -c, --continue-on-error / -C, --stop-on-error
                                     Continue processing other files if one fails [default: stop-on-error]
     --help                          Show this message and exit.

Migration from parse-and-upload
-------------------------------

The ``convert`` command replaces the deprecated ``parse-and-upload`` command. Use ``convert`` to save test results to a local file instead of uploading to a database.

.. code-block:: bash

   # Old command (deprecated)
   nvcomms-perf parse-and-upload /path/to/tarballs.tar.gz

   # New command
   nvcomms-perf convert -i tarball:/path/to/tarballs.tar.gz -o results.csv

Key Differences
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

1. **Purpose**: ``convert`` is for converting test results to a local file, not for uploading to a database.
2. **Input specification**: Explicit type required (e.g., ``tarball:`` or ``nccl-tests:``)
3. **Output specification**: Output must be specified with ``-o``, always creating a local file
4. **Multiple inputs**: Can process multiple test result sources in one command using multiple ``-i`` options
5. **Progress control**: Use ``--show-progress`` / ``--hide-progress``
6. **Error handling**: Use ``--continue-on-error`` / ``--stop-on-error``

Supported Formats
-----------------

- Input: NCCL test output, tarball
- Output: CSV (more formats may be added in the future)

Report Generation
=================

Overview
--------
The ``report`` command generates performance analysis reports from test results. It supports CSV files and tarballs as input, and produces PDF reports with various analysis types and visualizations.

Quick Start
-----------

.. code-block:: bash

    # Basic report with default settings
    nvcomms-perf report -i results.csv -o report.pdf

    # Comprehensive report with custom configuration
    nvcomms-perf report -i results.csv -o report.pdf --pdf-type comprehensive_report --plot-config custom_plot.toml --style-config custom_style.toml

Input Types
-----------
- **CSV Files**: Direct test result data
- **Tarballs**: Archives containing test results

Report Types
------------
The report generator offers two PDF report types:

Basic Report (``basic_report``)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
- Default report type
- Includes:
  - Basic collective operations analysis
  - Basic P2P operations analysis
- Uses default algorithm configurations
- Suitable for routine performance testing

Comprehensive Report (``comprehensive_report``)
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
- Advanced report type
- Includes:
  - Advanced collective operations analysis
  - Advanced P2P operations analysis
  - Algorithm comparisons
  - Detailed optimizations
- Suitable for performance tuning

Chart Types
-----------

Default Configuration Comparison
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Purpose:
    Compare performance with default algorithm and protocol settings

Fixed Parameters:
    - NCCL_ALGO = "DEFAULT"
    - NCCL_PROTO = "DEFAULT"
    - NCCL_MIN_CTAS = "DEFAULT"

Split Parameters:
    - num_nodes = "all"
    - num_processes = "all"
    - NCCL_TESTS_SPLIT_MASK = "all"

Combine Parameters:
    - local_register = "all"


Algorithm Comparison
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Purpose:
    Compare performance of different NCCL algorithms

Fixed Parameters:
    - NCCL_MIN_CTAS = "DEFAULT"

Split Parameters:
    - num_nodes = "all"
    - num_processes = "all"
    - NCCL_TESTS_SPLIT_MASK = "all"

Combine Parameters:
    - NCCL_ALGO = "all"
    - NCCL_PROTO = "all"
    - local_register = "all"


Scale Comparison
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Purpose:
    Compare performance across different node and process counts

Fixed Parameters:
    - NCCL_ALGO = "DEFAULT"
    - NCCL_PROTO = "DEFAULT"
    - NCCL_MIN_CTAS = "DEFAULT"

Split Parameters:
    - NCCL_TESTS_SPLIT_MASK = "all"

Combine Parameters:
    - num_nodes = "all"
    - num_processes = "all"
    - local_register = "all"

P2P Basic Comparison
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Purpose:
    Compare basic P2P performance with default configurations

Fixed Parameters:
    - NCCL_ALGO = "DEFAULT"
    - NCCL_PROTO = "DEFAULT"
    - NCCL_MIN_CTAS = "DEFAULT"

Split Parameters:
    - num_nodes = "all"
    - num_processes = "all"
    - NCCL_TESTS_SPLIT_MASK = "all"

Chart Type Parameter Configuration
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Chart parameters control how data is filtered and grouped:

- **Fixed Parameters**: Values that must match exactly (e.g., NCCL_ALGO="DEFAULT")
- **Split Parameters**: Each unique combination creates a separate chart
- **Combine Parameters**: All combinations appear within the same chart

Parameter Syntax and Behavior
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~``

**Fixed Parameters** (``[chart.fixed_params]``):
    Parameters with exact values that filter the data. Only data matching these exact values will be included in the chart.

    Syntax: ``parameter_name = "exact_value"``
    
    Example:
    - ``NCCL_ALGO = "DEFAULT"``: Only include data where NCCL_ALGO equals exactly "DEFAULT"
    - ``NCCL_PROTO = "DEFAULT"``: Only include data where NCCL_PROTO equals exactly "DEFAULT"
    - ``NCCL_MIN_CTAS = "DEFAULT"``: Only include data where NCCL_MIN_CTAS equals exactly "DEFAULT"

**Split Parameters** (``[chart.chart_split_params]``):
    Parameters that create separate charts. Each unique combination of these parameters generates its own chart.

    Syntax: ``parameter_name = "all"`` or ``parameter_name = ["value1", "value2", ...]``
    
    Examples:
    - ``num_nodes = "all"``: Create a separate chart for each unique number of nodes
    - ``num_processes = "all"``: Create a separate chart for each unique number of processes
    - ``NCCL_TESTS_SPLIT_MASK = "all"``: Create a separate chart for each unique split mask value

    Result: If you have data with 2 nodes, 3 process counts, and 2 split mask values, you'll get 2 × 3 × 2 = 12 separate charts.

**Combine Parameters** (``[chart.chart_combine_params]``):
    Parameters that are combined within the same chart. All combinations of these parameters appear as different lines/curves in the same chart.

    Syntax: ``parameter_name = "all"`` or ``parameter_name = ["value1", "value2", ...]``
    
    Examples:
    - ``local_register = "all"``: Show all register types as different lines in the same chart
    - ``NCCL_ALGO = "all"``: Show all algorithms as different lines in the same chart
    - ``NCCL_PROTO = "all"``: Show all protocols as different lines in the same chart

    Result: If you have data with 3 algorithms and 2 protocols, you'll get 3 × 2 = 6 different lines in the same chart.

Chart Type Parameter Interaction
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The three parameter types work together to control chart generation:

1. **Fixed parameters** filter the data first (only matching data is considered)
2. **Split parameters** determine how many charts are created
3. **Combine parameters** determine how many lines appear in each chart

**Important**: If no data matches the specified parameters, the parameter is ignored and the process continues. This ensures that reports can still be generated even if some expected data is missing.

Example scenario with the following configuration:
- Fixed: ``NCCL_ALGO = "DEFAULT"``
- Split: ``num_nodes = "all"``, ``num_processes = "all"``
- Combine: ``local_register = "all"``

If your data contains:
- 2 unique node counts (1, 2)
- 3 unique process counts (4, 8, 16)
- 2 unique register types (disabled, enabled)

Result:
- 2 × 3 = 6 charts will be created (one for each node/process combination)
- Each chart will have 2 lines (one for each register type)
- Only data with NCCL_ALGO="DEFAULT" will be included

**No Match Handling**:
- If no data has NCCL_ALGO="DEFAULT", the fixed parameter is ignored and all data is used
- If no data has a specific node count, that chart is simply not created
- If no data has a specific register type, that line is not shown in the chart

Upload Command
==============

Overview
--------

The ``upload`` command uploads test results to databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite) and/or S3 cloud storage. It provides a flexible way to store and manage performance test data for analysis and long-term storage.

Key Features
~~~~~~~~~~~~

- Upload to multiple storage backends simultaneously
- Support for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite databases
- S3-compatible object storage support
- Automatic deduplication to avoid duplicate uploads
- Progress tracking with detailed status updates
- Parallel processing for improved performance
- Environment variable support for credentials

Quick Start
-----------

Upload test results to various storage backends:

.. code-block:: bash

   # Upload to PostgreSQL database
   nvcomms-perf upload -i tarball:/path/to/test-results.tar.gz --db-url postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host:port/database

   # Upload to S3
   nvcomms-perf upload -i tarball:/path/to/test-results.tar.gz --s3-bucket my-bucket --s3-region us-east-1

   # Upload to both PostgreSQL and S3
   nvcomms-perf upload -i tarball:/path/to/test-results.tar.gz \
       --db-url postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host:port/database \
       --s3-bucket my-bucket --s3-region us-east-1

   # Upload multiple files
   nvcomms-perf upload -i tarball:/path/to/archive1.tar.gz -i tarball:/path/to/archive2.tar.gz \
       --db-url postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host:port/database

Command-line Interface
----------------------

Options
~~~~~~~

**Input Options:**

- ``-i, --input``: Input file(s) to upload. Supported types: nccl-tests, tarball [required]

**Database Options:**

- ``--db-url``: Database URL (e.g., postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host:port/db) [env: NVCOMMS_PERF_DB_URL]
- ``--db-schema``: Database schema to use (PostgreSQL only) [env: NVCOMMS_PERF_DB_SCHEMA]

**S3 Options:**

- ``--s3-bucket``: S3 bucket name [env: NVCOMMS_PERF_S3_BUCKET]
- ``--s3-region``: S3 region [env: NVCOMMS_PERF_S3_REGION]
- ``--s3-endpoint``: S3 endpoint URL (for S3-compatible services) [env: NVCOMMS_PERF_S3_ENDPOINT]
- ``--s3-access-key``: S3 access key ID [env: NVCOMMS_PERF_S3_ACCESS_KEY or AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID]
- ``--s3-secret-key``: S3 secret access key [env: NVCOMMS_PERF_S3_SECRET_KEY or AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY]

**Processing Options:**

- ``--max-workers``: Maximum number of parallel workers for parsing
- ``-p, --show-progress / -P, --hide-progress``: Show/hide progress bar [default: show]
- ``-c, --continue-on-error / -C, --stop-on-error``: Continue processing if a file fails [default: continue]

Database Configuration
----------------------

~~~~~~~~~~

.. code-block:: bash

   # Basic PostgreSQL connection
   nvcomms-perf upload -i tarball:/path/to/results.tar.gz \
       --db-url postgresql+psycopg://user:password@localhost:5432/perfdb

   # With specific schema
   nvcomms-perf upload -i tarball:/path/to/results.tar.gz \
       --db-url postgresql+psycopg://user:password@localhost:5432/perfdb \
       --db-schema performance_data

Advanced Usage
--------------

Deduplication
~~~~~~~~~~~~~

The upload command automatically checks for duplicate files:

1. **File-level deduplication**: Identical files are detected and skipped
2. **Database deduplication**: Files already in the database are skipped
3. **Hash-based detection**: Uses file content hash for accurate detection

.. code-block:: bash

   # Upload will skip files that already exist in the database
   nvcomms-perf upload -i tarball:/path/to/results.tar.gz \
       --db-url postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host/db

   # Output will show:
   # ⚠ file.tar.gz already exists in the database

Parallel Processing
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

.. code-block:: bash

   # Use custom number of workers for large uploads
   nvcomms-perf upload -i tarball:/path/to/large-dataset.tar.gz \
       --db-url postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host/db \
       --max-workers 16

   # Limit workers for resource-constrained environments
   nvcomms-perf upload -i tarball:/path/to/results.tar.gz \
       --db-url postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host/db \
       --max-workers 2

Error Handling
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

.. code-block:: bash

   # Stop on first error (default: continue)
   nvcomms-perf upload -i tarball:/path/to/results.tar.gz \
       --db-url postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host/db \
       --stop-on-error

   # Continue processing other files if one fails (default)
   nvcomms-perf upload -i tarball:/path/to/results.tar.gz \
       --db-url postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host/db \
       --continue-on-error

Combined Storage
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Upload to both database and S3 for redundancy:

.. code-block:: bash

   # Upload to both PostgreSQL and S3
   nvcomms-perf upload -i tarball:/path/to/results.tar.gz \
       --db-url postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host:5432/perfdb \
       --db-schema test_results \
       --s3-bucket perf-data-backup \
       --s3-region us-west-2

   # The database will store S3 paths for reference
   # raw_data_path: s3://perf-data-backup/uuid/filename.tar.gz

Environment Variables
---------------------

The upload command supports environment variables for all options:

.. code-block:: bash

   # Database configuration
   export NVCOMMS_PERF_DB_URL="postgresql+psycopg://user:pass@host:5432/perfdb"
   export NVCOMMS_PERF_DB_SCHEMA="performance"

   # S3 configuration
   export NVCOMMS_PERF_S3_BUCKET="my-perf-data"
   export NVCOMMS_PERF_S3_REGION="us-east-1"
   export NVCOMMS_PERF_S3_ENDPOINT="https://s3.amazonaws.com"
   export NVCOMMS_PERF_S3_ACCESS_KEY="your-access-key"
   export NVCOMMS_PERF_S3_SECRET_KEY="your-secret-key"

   # Or use standard AWS environment variables
   export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="your-access-key"
   export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="your-secret-key"

   # Now upload without specifying credentials
   nvcomms-perf upload -i tarball:/path/to/results.tar.gz

--------------

After upload completes, you'll see a detailed summary:

Best Practices
--------------

1. **Use environment variables** for credentials instead of command-line options
2. **Enable deduplication** by always using the same database for uploads
3. **Use S3 for raw data** and database for structured/searchable data
4. **Set appropriate worker counts** based on your system resources
5. **Monitor progress** with ``--show-progress`` for large uploads
6. **Use schemas** in PostgreSQL to organize data by project or team

def _convert_nccl_version(version: Optional[int]) -> Optional[str]:
    """
    Convert NCCL version from numeric format to semantic version (X.Y.Z).

    The numeric format is calculated as:
    `#define NCCL_VERSION(X,Y,Z) (((X) <= 2 && (Y) <= 8) ? (X) * 1000 + (Y) * 100 + (Z) : (X) * 10000 + (Y) * 100 + (Z))`
    - For X <= 2 and Y <= 8: X * 1000 + Y * 100 + Z
    - For other cases: X * 10000 + Y * 100 + Z

    Examples:
    - 22702 -> 2.27.2
    - 21800 -> 2.18.0
    """
    if version is None:
        return None

    if version <= 2800:  # X <= 2 and Y <= 8 case
        x = version // 1000
        y = (version % 1000) // 100
        z = version % 100
    else:  # X * 10000 + Y * 100 + Z case
        x = version // 10000
        y = (version % 10000) // 100
        z = version % 100

    return f"{x}.{y}.{z}"

        import argparse

        def parse_size(value: str) -> int:
            """Parse size values with optional suffixes (K, M, G)."""
            # Match the C parsesize function behavior
            value = value.strip()
            if not value:
                return 0

            # Try to parse as "number suffix" format
            import re

            match = re.match(r"^(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*([KMGkmg]?)$", value)
            if match:
                size = float(match.group(1))
                suffix = match.group(2).upper() if match.group(2) else ""

                if suffix == "K":
                    return int(size * 1024)
                elif suffix == "M":
                    return int(size * 1024 * 1024)
                elif suffix == "G":
                    return int(size * 1024 * 1024 * 1024)
                else:
                    return int(size)

            # Fallback to simple int parsing
            try:
                return int(value, 0)
            except ValueError:
                raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(f"invalid size specified: {value}")

        def parse_int(value: str) -> int:
            """Parse int values, supporting decimal, hex (0x), and octal (0) formats."""
            # Match C's strtol behavior with base 0
            value = value.strip()
            if value.startswith("0x") or value.startswith("0X"):
                return int(value, 16)
            elif value.startswith("0") and len(value) > 1 and value[1].isdigit():
                return int(value, 8)
            else:
                return int(value, 10)

        def parse_bool(value: str) -> bool:
            """Parse boolean values from 0/1."""
            int_val = parse_int(value)
            return bool(int_val)

        def parse_local_register(value: str) -> str:
            """Parse -R option following NCCL's logic."""
            # Match the C implementation from NCCL
            if value and value[0] == "s":
                return "LOCAL_REGISTER_SEND"
            elif value and value[0] == "r":
                return "LOCAL_REGISTER_RECV"
            elif value and value[0] == "a":
                return "LOCAL_REGISTER_ALL"  # LOCAL_REGISTER_SEND|LOCAL_REGISTER_RECV
            else:
                # Try to parse as int
                try:
                    # Use the same logic as parse_int for consistent int parsing
                    value = value.strip()
                    if value.startswith("0x") or value.startswith("0X"):
                        int_val = int(value, 16)
                    elif value.startswith("0") and len(value) > 1 and value[1].isdigit():
                        int_val = int(value, 8)
                    else:
                        int_val = int(value, 10)

                    if int_val == 0:
                        return "disabled"
                    elif int_val == 1:
                        return "LOCAL_REGISTER_ALL"  # LOCAL_REGISTER_SEND|LOCAL_REGISTER_RECV
                    elif int_val == 2:
                        return "SYMMETRIC_REGISTER_ALL"
                    else:
                        return str(int_val)  # For other values, return as string
                except ValueError:
                    return value

        # Split the command string and skip the executable
        args_list = shlex.split(args)[1:]  # Skip executable

        # Create parser with add_help=False to handle -h ourselves
        parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)

        # Add all arguments
        parser.add_argument("-t", "--nthreads", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-g", "--ngpus", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-b", "--minbytes", type=parse_size)
        parser.add_argument("-e", "--maxbytes", type=parse_size)
        parser.add_argument("-i", "--stepbytes", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-f", "--stepfactor", type=float)
        parser.add_argument("-s", "--tbytes", type=parse_size)
        parser.add_argument("-n", "--iters", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-m", "--agg_iters", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-w", "--warmup_iters", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-N", "--run_cycles", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-p", "--parallel_init", type=parse_bool)
        parser.add_argument("-c", "--check", type=parse_bool)
        parser.add_argument("-o", "--op", type=str)
        parser.add_argument("-d", "--datatype", type=str)
        parser.add_argument("-r", "--root", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-z", "--blocking", type=parse_bool)
        parser.add_argument("-y", "--stream_null", type=parse_bool)
        parser.add_argument("-k", "--side_comp", type=parse_bool)
        parser.add_argument("-l", "--replay", type=str)
        parser.add_argument("-T", "--timeout", type=float)
        parser.add_argument("-G", "--cudagraph", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-C", "--report_cputime", type=parse_bool)
        parser.add_argument("-O", "--out_of_place", type=parse_bool)
        parser.add_argument("-u", "--unalign", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-J", "--output_file", type=str)
        parser.add_argument("-a", "--average", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-B", "--commblocking", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-F", "--ft_test", type=parse_bool)
        parser.add_argument("-L", "--ft_list", type=str)
        parser.add_argument("-S", "--split_share", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-P", "--split_comm", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-R", "--local_register", type=parse_local_register)
        parser.add_argument("-A", "--per_coll_perf", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-E", "--simulate", type=parse_bool)
        parser.add_argument("-I", "--init_ids", type=str)
        parser.add_argument("-q", "--traffic_class", type=parse_int)
        parser.add_argument("-h", "--help", action="store_true")

        try:
            # Parse known args (ignore unknown ones)
            parsed_args, _ = parser.parse_known_args(args_list)

            # Convert to dict, using short option names for validation
            parsed_dict = {}
            for short_opt, long_opt in [
                ("t", "nthreads"),
                ("g", "ngpus"),
                ("b", "minbytes"),
                ("e", "maxbytes"),
                ("i", "stepbytes"),
                ("f", "stepfactor"),
                ("s", "tbytes"),
                ("n", "iters"),
                ("m", "agg_iters"),
                ("w", "warmup_iters"),
                ("N", "run_cycles"),
                ("p", "parallel_init"),
                ("c", "check"),
                ("o", "op"),
                ("d", "datatype"),
                ("r", "root"),
                ("z", "blocking"),
                ("y", "stream_null"),
                ("k", "side_comp"),
                ("l", "replay"),
                ("T", "timeout"),
                ("G", "cudagraph"),
                ("C", "report_cputime"),
                ("O", "out_of_place"),
                ("u", "unalign"),
                ("J", "output_file"),
                ("a", "average"),
                ("B", "commblocking"),
                ("F", "ft_test"),
                ("L", "ft_list"),
                ("S", "split_share"),
                ("P", "split_comm"),
                ("R", "local_register"),
                ("A", "per_coll_perf"),
                ("E", "simulate"),
                ("I", "init_ids"),
                ("q", "traffic_class"),
                ("h", "help"),
            ]:
                value = getattr(parsed_args, long_opt, None)
                if value is not None:
                    parsed_dict[short_opt] = value

            return cls.model_validate(parsed_dict)

        except (argparse.ArgumentError, SystemExit):
            # If argparse fails, return empty options
            return cls()

class NcclTestResult(BaseModel):
    """
    Represents the result of an nccl-tests run.

    Note:
        Recommend to use the provided properties (`test_config`, `device_list`, `result_dataframe`, etc.) to access relevant data.
    """

    start_time: Optional[datetime] = None
    end_time: Optional[datetime] = None
    args: Annotated[Optional[str], BeforeValidator(lambda x: None if x is None else shlex.join(x) if isinstance(x, list) else x), Field(default=None)]
    env: Annotated[
        Optional[dict[str, str]],
        BeforeValidator(lambda x: {k: v for k, v in (item.split("=", 1) for item in x)} if x else None),
    ] = None
    nccl_version: Annotated[Optional[str], BeforeValidator(_convert_nccl_version)] = None

    config: NcclTestConfig
    results: list[NcclTestBenchmarkRow]

    out_of_bounds: NcclTestOutOfBound
    average_bus_bandwidth: NcclTestAvgBusBw = Field(validation_alias="average_bus_bandwidith")

    errors: Optional[list[str]] = None

    @computed_field
    @property
    def cmd_options(self) -> Optional[NcclTestCmdOptions]:
        if not self.args:
            return None

        # self.args is always a string due to BeforeValidator
        return NcclTestCmdOptions.from_args(self.args)

    model_config = ConfigDict(
        extra="ignore",
        frozen=True,
        validate_by_alias=True,
        validate_by_name=True,
        serialize_by_alias=False,
    )

    @model_validator(mode="after")
    def validate_num_benchmark_rows(self):
        cfg = self.config
        import math

        if cfg.step_type == "factor":
            if cfg.step <= 1:
                raise ValueError(f"Step must be > 1 for factor step_type, got {cfg.step}")
            expected = math.floor(math.log(cfg.max_bytes / cfg.min_bytes, cfg.step)) + 1
            actual = len(self.results)
            if actual != expected:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Expected {expected} benchmark rows for maxBytes {cfg.max_bytes}, minBytes {cfg.min_bytes}, step: {cfg.step}({cfg.step_type}), but got {actual}."
                )
        elif cfg.step_type == "bytes":
            if cfg.step <= 0:
                raise ValueError(f"Step must be > 0 for bytes step_type, got {cfg.step}")
            expected = math.floor((cfg.max_bytes - cfg.min_bytes) / cfg.step) + 1
            actual = len(self.results)
            if actual != expected:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Expected {expected} benchmark rows for maxBytes {cfg.max_bytes}, minBytes {cfg.min_bytes}, step: {cfg.step}({cfg.step_type}), but got {actual}."
                )
        return self

    @classmethod
    def read_json(cls, obj: Union[str, bytes, bytearray, memoryview, IO]) -> "NcclTestResult":
        """
        Parse a NcclTestResult from JSON content.

        Accepts:
        - str: JSON string
        - bytes: JSON content as bytes
        - file-like object: Any object with a .read() method
        """
        if isinstance(obj, (str, bytes)):
            return cls.model_validate_json(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, (bytearray, memoryview)):
            return cls.model_validate_json(bytes(obj))
        elif hasattr(obj, "read"):
            return cls.model_validate_json(obj.read())
        else:
            raise TypeError(
                "Unsupported input type for read_json; must be str, bytes, bytearray, memoryview, or file-like object."
            )

    @classmethod
    def read_plain_output(cls, obj: Union[str, bytes, bytearray, memoryview, IO]) -> "NcclTestResult":
        """
        Parse a NcclTestResult from plain text NCCL test output.

        Accepts:
        - str: plain text output
        - bytes: plain text as bytes
        - bytearray, memoryview: plain text as bytes-like
        - file-like object: Any object with a .read() method
        """
        if isinstance(obj, str):
            return cls._read_plain_output_str(obj)
        elif isinstance(obj, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
            return cls._read_plain_output_str(bytes(obj).decode())
        elif hasattr(obj, "read"):
            content = obj.read()
            if isinstance(content, bytes):
                content = content.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            return cls._read_plain_output_str(content)
        else:
            raise TypeError(
                "Unsupported input type for read_plain_output; must be str, bytes, bytearray, memoryview, or file-like object."
            )

    @classmethod
    def _read_plain_output_str(cls, output: str) -> "NcclTestResult":
        """
        Parse a NcclTestResult from a plain text NCCL test output string.

        Args:
            output (str): Plain text output from an NCCL test.

        Returns:
            NcclTestResult: Parsed result object.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If the string cannot be parsed as a valid NCCL test output.
        """
        all_lines = output.splitlines()

        arguments_pattern = re.compile(
            r"\#\s+nThread\s+(?P<n_threads>\d+)\s+nGpus\s+(?P<n_gpus>\d+)\s+minBytes\s+(?P<min_bytes>\d+)\s+maxBytes\s+(?P<max_bytes>\d+)\s+"
            r"step:\s+(?P<step>\d+)\((?P<step_type>factor|bytes)\)\s+warmup\s+iters:\s+(?P<warmup_iters>\d+)\s+iters:\s+(?P<iters>\d+)\s+"
            r"agg iters:\s+(?P<agg_iters>\d+)\s+validation:\s+(?P<validation>\d+)\s+graph:\s+(?P<graph>\d+)"
        )
        device_info_pattern = re.compile(
            r"\#\s+Rank\s+(?P<rank>\d+)\s+Group\s+(?P<group>\d+)\s+Pid\s+(?P<pid>\d+)\s+on\s+(?P<hostname>\S+)\s+"
            r"device\s+(?P<device>\d+)\s+\[(?P<device_hex>\S+)\]\s+(?P<device_info>.+)"
        )
        result_header_pattern = re.compile(
            r"#\s+size\s+count\s+type\s+redop\s+root\s+time\s+algbw\s+busbw\s+#wrong\s+time\s+algbw\s+busbw\s+#wrong"
        )
        result_header_ex_pattern = re.compile(
            r"#\s+size\s+count\s+type\s+redop\s+root\s+timeAvg\s+algbwAvg\s+busbwAvg\s+timeMax\s+algbwMax\s+busbwMax\s+#wrong\s+timeAvg\s+algbwAvg\s+busbwAvg\s+timeMax\s+algbwMax\s+busbwMax\s+#wrong"
        )
        result_values_pattern = re.compile(
            r"\s+(?P<size>\d+)\s+(?P<count>\d+)\s+(?P<type>[a-zA-Z0-9]+)\s+(?P<redop>[a-zA-Z]+)\s+(?P<root>-?\d+)\s+"
            r"(?P<oop_time>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<oop_algbw>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<oop_busbw>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<oop_wrong>[^\s]+)\s+"
            r"(?P<inp_time>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<inp_algbw>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<inp_busbw>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<inp_wrong>[^\s]+)"
            r"(?:\s+(?P<actual_iterations>\d+))?(?:\s+(?P<experiment_name>.+))?"
        )
        result_values_ex_pattern = re.compile(
            r"\s+(?P<size>\d+)\s+(?P<count>\d+)\s+(?P<type>[a-zA-Z0-9]+)\s+(?P<redop>[a-zA-Z]+)\s+(?P<root>-?\d+)\s+"
            r"(?P<oop_time>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<oop_algbw>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<oop_busbw>[^\s]+)\s+"
            r"(?P<oop_timeMax>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<oop_algbwMax>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<oop_busbwMax>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<oop_wrong>[^\s]+)\s+"
            r"(?P<inp_time>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<inp_algbw>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<inp_busbw>[^\s]+)\s*"
            r"(?P<inp_timeMax>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<inp_algbwMax>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<inp_busbwMax>[^\s]+)\s+(?P<inp_wrong>[^\s]+)"
            r"(?:\s+(?P<actual_iterations>\d+))?(?:\s+(?P<experiment_name>.+))?"
        )
        out_of_bounds_pattern = re.compile(r"# Out of bounds values\s+:\s+(?P<count>\d+)\s+(?P<okay>OK|FAILED)")
        avg_bus_bandwidth_pattern = re.compile(
            r"# Avg bus bandwidth\s+:\s+(?P<bandwidth>[^\s]+)(?:\s+(?P<okay>OK|FAILED))?"
        )

        arguments = next((match.groupdict() for line in all_lines if (match := arguments_pattern.match(line))), {})
        if not arguments:
            raise ValueError("Failed to parse nccl tests output: arguments not found")

        device_list = [match.groupdict() for line in all_lines if (match := device_info_pattern.match(line))]
        if not device_list:
            raise ValueError("Failed to parse nccl tests output: device list not found")

        if any((match := result_header_pattern.match(line)) for line in all_lines):
            result_values = [match.groupdict() for line in all_lines if (match := result_values_pattern.match(line))]
            if not result_values:
                raise ValueError("Failed to parse nccl tests output: result values not found")
        elif any((match := result_header_ex_pattern.match(line)) for line in all_lines):
            result_values = [match.groupdict() for line in all_lines if (match := result_values_ex_pattern.match(line))]
            if not result_values:
                raise ValueError("Failed to parse nccl tests output: result values (extended) not found")
        else:
            raise ValueError("Failed to parse nccl tests output: result header not found")

        oob_values = next((match.groupdict() for line in all_lines if (match := out_of_bounds_pattern.match(line))), {})
        if not oob_values:
            raise ValueError("Failed to parse nccl tests output: out of bounds values not found")

        avg_bus_bandwidth = next(
            (match.groupdict() for line in all_lines if (match := avg_bus_bandwidth_pattern.match(line))), {}
        )
        if not avg_bus_bandwidth:
            raise ValueError("Failed to parse nccl tests output: average bus bandwidth not found")

        config = NcclTestConfig.model_validate(
            {**arguments, "devices": [NcclTestDevice.model_validate(d) for d in device_list]}
        )

        results = []
        for r in result_values:
            row_dict = {
                "size": r["size"],
                "count": r["count"],
                "type": r["type"],
                "redop": r["redop"],
                "root": r["root"],
                "out_of_place": NcclTestBenchmark.model_validate(
                    {
                        "time": r["oop_time"],
                        "alg_bw": r["oop_algbw"],
                        "bus_bw": r["oop_busbw"],
                        "time_max": r.get("oop_timeMax", None),
                        "alg_bw_max": r.get("oop_algbwMax", None),
                        "bus_bw_max": r.get("oop_busbwMax", None),
                        "nwrong": r["oop_wrong"].strip(),
                    }
                ),
                "in_place": NcclTestBenchmark.model_validate(
                    {
                        "time": r["inp_time"],
                        "alg_bw": r["inp_algbw"],
                        "bus_bw": r["inp_busbw"],
                        "time_max": r.get("inp_timeMax", None),
                        "alg_bw_max": r.get("inp_algbwMax", None),
                        "bus_bw_max": r.get("inp_busbwMax", None),
                        "nwrong": r["inp_wrong"].strip(),
                    }
                ),
                "actual_iterations": r.get("actual_iterations", None),
                "experiment_name": r.get("experiment_name", None),
            }
            benchmark_row = NcclTestBenchmarkRow.model_validate(row_dict)
            results.append(benchmark_row)

        test_result = cls.model_validate(
            {
                "config": config,
                "results": results,
                "out_of_bounds": NcclTestOutOfBound.model_validate(oob_values),
                "average_bus_bandwidth": NcclTestAvgBusBw.model_validate(avg_bus_bandwidth),
            }
        )

        return test_result

class TestMetadata(BaseModel):
    test_name: str
    log_name: str

    container: Optional[str] = None
    num_nodes: int
    num_processes: int
    num_process_per_node: int

    slurm_id: Optional[int] = None
    slurm_job_name: Optional[str] = None

    @computed_field
    @property
    def env(self) -> Optional[dict[str, str]]:
        if match := re.search(r"env (.+?) bash -c ", self.cmd):
            env_part = match.group(1)
            return {k: v for k, v in (item.strip().split("=", 1) for item in env_part.split("env"))}

        return None

    model_config = ConfigDict(
        extra="allow",
        frozen=True,

    @classmethod
    def read_yaml(cls, obj: Union[str, bytes, IO]) -> "TestMetadata":
        """
        Parse YAML content into a TestMetadata instance.

        Accepts:
        - str: YAML content as a string (not a file path)
        - bytes: YAML content as bytes (passed directly to yaml.safe_load)
        - file-like object: Any object with a .read() method

        This mimics yaml.safe_load behavior: both str and bytes are treated as YAML content, not as file paths.
        """
        if isinstance(obj, (str, bytes)):
            # Treat as YAML content (not a file path)
            return cls.model_validate(yaml.safe_load(obj))
        elif hasattr(obj, "read"):
            # File-like object
            return cls.model_validate(yaml.safe_load(obj))
        else:
            raise TypeError("Unsupported input type for read_yaml; must be str, bytes, or file-like object.")

"""
Tests for plot configuration validation, specifically parameter conflict detection.
"""

import pytest
import tempfile
import os
from pydantic import ValidationError

from nvcomms_perf.report.models.plot_config import ChartType, ChartConfigLoader


class TestParameterConflictValidation:
    """Test parameter conflict validation in ChartType configuration."""

    def test_valid_chart_type_no_conflicts(self):
        """Test that a valid chart type with no parameter conflicts passes validation."""
        chart_config = {
            "id": "test_chart",
            "name": "test_chart",
            "description": "Test chart",
            "fixed_params": {"param1": "value1"},
            "chart_split_params": {"param2": "all"},
            "chart_combine_params": {"param3": "all"}
        }

        chart = ChartType(**chart_config)  # type: ignore
        assert chart.name == "test_chart"
        assert chart.fixed_params == {"param1": "value1"}
        assert chart.chart_split_params == {"param2": "all"}
        assert chart.chart_combine_params == {"param3": "all"}

    def test_fixed_and_split_param_conflict(self):
        """Test that a conflict between fixed_params and chart_split_params raises an error."""
        chart_config = {
            "id": "conflict_chart",
            "name": "conflict_chart",
            "description": "Chart with parameter conflict",
            "fixed_params": {"param1": "value1"},
            "chart_split_params": {"param1": "all"},  # Same parameter as fixed_params
            "chart_combine_params": {"param2": "all"}
        }

        with pytest.raises(ValidationError) as exc_info:
            ChartType(**chart_config)

        error_message = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "parameter conflicts" in error_message
        assert "param1" in error_message
        assert "fixed_params and chart_split_params" in error_message

    def test_fixed_and_combine_param_conflict(self):
        """Test that a conflict between fixed_params and chart_combine_params raises an error."""
        chart_config = {
            "id": "conflict_chart",
            "name": "conflict_chart",
            "description": "Chart with parameter conflict",
            "fixed_params": {"param1": "value1"},
            "chart_split_params": {"param2": "all"},
            "chart_combine_params": {"param1": "all"}  # Same parameter as fixed_params
        }

        with pytest.raises(ValidationError) as exc_info:
            ChartType(**chart_config)

        error_message = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "parameter conflicts" in error_message
        assert "param1" in error_message
        assert "fixed_params and chart_combine_params" in error_message

    def test_split_and_combine_param_conflict(self):

        chart_config = {

            "name": "conflict_chart",

            "chart_split_params": {"param2": "all"},
            "chart_combine_params": {"param2": "all"}  # Same parameter as chart_split_params
        }

        with pytest.raises(ValidationError) as exc_info:

        error_message = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "parameter conflicts" in error_message
        assert "param2" in error_message
        assert "chart_split_params and chart_combine_params" in error_message

            "id": "multiple_conflicts",
            "name": "multiple_conflicts",
            "description": "Chart with multiple parameter conflicts",
            "fixed_params": {"param1": "value1", "param2": "value2"},

            "chart_combine_params": {"param2": "all"}  # Same parameter as default_values
        }

        with pytest.raises(ValidationError) as exc_info:
            ChartType(**chart_config)

        error_message = str(exc_info.value)
        assert "parameter conflicts" in error_message
        assert "param2" in error_message
        assert "chart_combine_params and default_values" in error_message

    def test_toml_file_with_conflicts(self):
        """Test that validation catches conflicts in TOML file loading."""
        # Create a temporary TOML file with parameter conflicts
        problematic_toml = """
[[chart]]
id = "conflict_test"
name = "Conflict Test Chart"
description = "Chart with parameter conflicts"
performance_columns = ["max_bus_bw"]

[chart.fixed_params]
NCCL_ALGO = "DEFAULT"

[chart.chart_split_params]
NCCL_ALGO = "all"  # Conflict: same parameter in fixed_params and chart_split_params

[chart.chart_combine_params]
local_register = "all"
"""

        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', suffix='.toml', delete=False) as f:
            f.write(problematic_toml)
            temp_file = f.name

        try:
            with pytest.raises(ValidationError) as exc_info:
                ChartConfigLoader.load_from_toml(temp_file)

            error_message = str(exc_info.value)
            assert "parameter conflicts" in error_message
            assert "NCCL_ALGO" in error_message
            assert "fixed_params and chart_split_params" in error_message

        finally:
            # Clean up temporary file
            if os.path.exists(temp_file):
                os.unlink(temp_file)

"""
API module for direct report generation.

This module provides clean interfaces for users to make direct API calls
to generate reports without using the CLI interface.
"""

import pandas as pd
import io
import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional, Union, Dict, Any, IO
import tempfile

from .models import ChartConfigLoader, StyleConfigLoader
from .adapters.nccl_adapter import NCCLPerformanceAdapter
from .generators.pdf import generate_pdf_report

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class ReportAPI:
    """API class for generating performance reports directly from data."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._default_plot_config = None
        self._default_style_config = None

    @staticmethod
    def _parse_dataframe_from_input(dataframe_input: Union[str, bytes, bytearray, memoryview, IO]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Parse DataFrame from various input types.

        Args:
            dataframe_input: Input data as string, bytes, or file-like object

        Returns:
            Parsed pandas DataFrame

        Raises:
            TypeError: If input type is not supported
        """
        if isinstance(dataframe_input, str):
            return pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(dataframe_input))
        elif isinstance(dataframe_input, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
            return pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(bytes(dataframe_input).decode()))
        elif hasattr(dataframe_input, 'read'):
            content = dataframe_input.read()
            if isinstance(content, bytes):
                content = content.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            return pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(content))
        else:
            raise TypeError("Unsupported input type for DataFrame parsing; must be str, bytes, bytearray, memoryview, or file-like object.")

    @staticmethod
    def _parse_config_from_input(config_input: Union[str, bytes, bytearray, memoryview, IO], config_type: str) -> Any:
        """Parse configuration from various input types.

        Args:
            config_input: Configuration input as string, bytes, or file-like object
            config_type: Type of configuration ('plot' or 'style')

        Returns:
            Parsed configuration object

        Raises:
            TypeError: If input type is not supported
            ValueError: If config_type is unknown
        """
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode='w', suffix='.toml', delete=False) as temp_file:
            if isinstance(config_input, str):
                temp_file.write(config_input)
            elif isinstance(config_input, (bytes, bytearray, memoryview)):
                temp_file.write(bytes(config_input).decode())
            elif hasattr(config_input, 'read'):
                content = config_input.read()
                if isinstance(content, bytes):
                    content = content.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
                temp_file.write(content)
            else:
                raise TypeError("Unsupported input type for config parsing; must be str, bytes, bytearray, memoryview, or file-like object.")
            temp_file_path = temp_file.name
        try:
            if config_type == 'plot':
                return ChartConfigLoader.load_from_toml(temp_file_path)
            elif config_type == 'style':
                return StyleConfigLoader.load_from_toml(temp_file_path)
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown config type: {config_type}")
        finally:
            Path(temp_file_path).unlink(missing_ok=True)

    def _load_default_configs(self):
        """Load default configurations if not already loaded."""
        if self._default_plot_config is None:
            from .cli.report import _get_default_config_path
            default_plot_path = _get_default_config_path('plot')
            self._default_plot_config = ChartConfigLoader.load_from_toml(str(default_plot_path))
        if self._default_style_config is None:
            from .cli.report import _get_default_config_path
            default_style_path = _get_default_config_path('style')
            self._default_style_config = StyleConfigLoader.load_from_toml(str(default_style_path))

    def generate_pdf_report_from_input(
        self,
        dataframe_input: Union[str, bytes, bytearray, memoryview, IO],
        output_path: Union[str, Path],
        pdf_type: str = "basic_report",
        plot_config_input: Optional[Union[str, bytes, bytearray, memoryview, IO]] = None,
        style_config_input: Optional[Union[str, bytes, bytearray, memoryview, IO]] = None,
        include_empty_pages: bool = True,
        include_data_tables: bool = True,
        include_test_commands: bool = True
    ) -> None:
        """Generate PDF report from various input types.

        Args:
            dataframe_input: DataFrame input as string, bytes, or file-like object
            output_path: Path where the PDF should be saved
            pdf_type: Type of PDF report to generate
            plot_config_input: Optional plot configuration input
            style_config_input: Optional style configuration input
            include_empty_pages: Whether to include empty lined pages
            include_data_tables: Whether to include data tables
            include_test_commands: Whether to include test command pages

        Raises:
            Exception: If PDF generation fails
        """
        logger.info("Generating PDF report from DataFrame input")
        logger.info(f"Output path: {output_path}")
        logger.info(f"PDF type: {pdf_type}")

        try:
            dataframe = self._parse_dataframe_from_input(dataframe_input)

            if plot_config_input:
                plot_config = self._parse_config_from_input(plot_config_input, 'plot')
            else:
                self._load_default_configs()
                plot_config = self._default_plot_config

            if style_config_input:
                style_config = self._parse_config_from_input(style_config_input, 'style')
            else:
                self._load_default_configs()
                style_config = self._default_style_config

            adapter = NCCLPerformanceAdapter(plot_config=plot_config, style_config=style_config)
            output_path = Path(output_path)

            generate_pdf_report(
                dataframe=dataframe,
                output_path=output_path,
                pdf_type=pdf_type,
                adapter=adapter,
                include_empty_pages=include_empty_pages,
                include_data_tables=include_data_tables,
                include_test_commands=include_test_commands
            )
            logger.info(f"Successfully generated PDF report: {output_path}")
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Failed to generate PDF report: {e}")
            raise

    def validate_dataframe_input(self, dataframe_input: Union[str, bytes, bytearray, memoryview, IO]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Validate DataFrame input and return metadata.

        Args:
            dataframe_input: DataFrame input to validate

        Returns:
            Dictionary with validation results and metadata
        """
        try:
            df = self._parse_dataframe_from_input(dataframe_input)
            return {
                'valid': True,
                'shape': df.shape,
                'columns': list(df.columns),
                'memory_usage_mb': df.memory_usage(deep=True).sum() / 1024 / 1024,
                'dtypes': df.dtypes.to_dict()
            }
        except Exception as e:
            return {'valid': False, 'error': str(e)}

class PydanticType(TypeDecorator):
    """SQLAlchemy type to store Pydantic models as JSON"""

    impl = json_type
    cache_ok = True

    def __init__(self, pydantic_type: Type[BaseModel], *args, **kwargs) -> None:
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        self._pydantic_type = pydantic_type

    def process_bind_param(self, value, dialect) -> Union[dict[str, Any], Any, None]:
        if value is not None:
            if isinstance(value, BaseModel):
                # Use mode='json' to handle datetime serialization properly
                return value.model_dump(mode="json")
            elif isinstance(value, dict):
                # Validate the dict by creating a Pydantic model, then return the dict
                return self._pydantic_type(**value).model_dump(mode="json")
            return value
        return value

    def process_result_value(self, value, dialect) -> Optional[BaseModel]:
        if value is not None:
            return self._pydantic_type(**value)
        return value

    def copy(self, **kw) -> "PydanticType":
        """Produce a copy of this PydanticType instance."""
        return self.__class__(self._pydantic_type, **kw)

class ChartType(BaseModel):
    """Chart type configuration."""

    id: str = Field(..., description="Unique chart type identifier")
    name: str = Field(..., description="Chart type name")
    description: str = Field(..., description="Chart type description")
    performance_columns: Optional[List[str]] = Field(
        None,
        description="Performance columns to plot"
    )
    fixed_params: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Fixed parameter values"
    )
    default_values: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Default parameter values"
    )
    chart_split_params: Optional[Dict[str, Union[str, List[str]]]] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Parameters to split charts by"
    )
    chart_combine_params: Optional[Dict[str, Union[str, List[str]]]] = Field(
        default_factory=dict,
        description="Parameters to combine in charts"
    )

    @model_validator(mode='after')
    def validate_parameter_conflicts(self):
        """Validate that parameters are not repeated between fixed_params, default_values, chart_split_params, and chart_combine_params."""
        fixed_params = set(self.fixed_params.keys()) if self.fixed_params else set()
        default_values = set(self.default_values.keys()) if self.default_values else set()
        split_params = set(self.chart_split_params.keys()) if self.chart_split_params else set()
        combine_params = set(self.chart_combine_params.keys()) if self.chart_combine_params else set()

        # Check for conflicts between fixed_params and split_params
        fixed_split_conflict = fixed_params & split_params
        if fixed_split_conflict:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Chart type '{self.name}' has parameter conflicts: "
                f"parameters {fixed_split_conflict} appear in both fixed_params and chart_split_params. "
                f"A parameter cannot be both fixed and used for splitting charts."
            )

        # Check for conflicts between fixed_params and combine_params
        fixed_combine_conflict = fixed_params & combine_params
        if fixed_combine_conflict:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Chart type '{self.name}' has parameter conflicts: "
                f"parameters {fixed_combine_conflict} appear in both fixed_params and chart_combine_params. "
                f"A parameter cannot be both fixed and used for combining in charts."
            )

        # Check for conflicts between fixed_params and default_values
        fixed_default_conflict = fixed_params & default_values
        if fixed_default_conflict:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Chart type '{self.name}' has parameter conflicts: "
                f"parameters {fixed_default_conflict} appear in both fixed_params and default_values. "
                f"A parameter cannot be both fixed and have a default value."
            )

        # Check for conflicts between split_params and combine_params
        split_combine_conflict = split_params & combine_params
        if split_combine_conflict:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Chart type '{self.name}' has parameter conflicts: "
                f"parameters {split_combine_conflict} appear in both chart_split_params and chart_combine_params. "
                f"A parameter cannot be used for both splitting charts and combining in charts."
            )

        # Check for conflicts between split_params and default_values
        split_default_conflict = split_params & default_values
        if split_default_conflict:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Chart type '{self.name}' has parameter conflicts: "
                f"parameters {split_default_conflict} appear in both chart_split_params and default_values. "
                f"A parameter cannot be used for splitting charts and have a default value."
            )

        # Check for conflicts between combine_params and default_values
        combine_default_conflict = combine_params & default_values
        if combine_default_conflict:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Chart type '{self.name}' has parameter conflicts: "
                f"parameters {combine_default_conflict} appear in both chart_combine_params and default_values. "
                f"A parameter cannot be used for combining in charts and have a default value."
            )

        return self
